description: The Settings dialog's Dependencies page (Baude's, Record's and the phone's; on the phone the third page of Settings, switched to by the bar at its foot): what the host picked beside New session and its machine's apps need, and the checks of what's installed (a kubeconfig's contexts, gh signed in, Ollama running and its models, MLX's models), each with what's said of it while it's there or the command that installs or readies it on that host, under a heading for what needs it. All of it but the libraries the app itself runs is the host's deps request's answer (schema/deps lists them, how each is looked for on macOS and Linux, its group, and its command per platform), so every app shows the same for the same host. The rows for what the app's own process needs (VTE, WebKit and WebKitGTK, Node.js: where "app" in schema/deps) are the viewing app's own look, not the host's, on Baude and Record, under the same groups; the phone runs none of them and shows none.
opens: Settings… → Dependencies (the dialog's page switcher; the phone's: the bar at Settings' foot)

parts.name: Host
parts.shows: Row "Host" with the picked host's name after it (a computer host: the phone runs none of these).

parts.name: groups
parts.shows: A heading and a boxed list for each thing that needs them, in this order, a group shown only when it has a row on that host: Providers (Antigravity CLI, Claude Code, Codex CLI, MLX on macOS, Ollama), Git and GitHub (Git, GitHub CLI, GitHub Account), Kubernetes (kubectl, kubeconfig), Databases (Docker), Multiplex (VTE; Xvfb on a Linux host with no display), Emission (WebKitGTK on Linux, WebKit on macOS), Signal (Node.js), Telemetry (line_profiler). In a group, rows go by name, a check (kubeconfig, GitHub Account) right after its program, and left out while its program isn't installed. The host's error, if it can't be asked, in the groups' place.

parts.name: dependency row
parts.shows: The program's name (its own spelling: kubectl), then, while it's there, what the host says of it (dim): "Installed", "Signed in" (GitHub Account), "2 contexts" (kubeconfig), "Running, 3 models" (Ollama), "2 models" (MLX, the downloaded ones); else the command that installs it on that host, or readies it (gh auth login; ollama serve for an Ollama that's installed and not running), in monospace (the phone's wraps to two lines) with a Copy button; else, with no command, an Install Page link for a program, and nothing more for a check (kubeconfig, GitHub Account: its status only); "Couldn't check" when looking at it failed, and "Running, needs a key" for an Ollama that wants a key.

parts.name: Deciders
parts.shows: The page's last group, under the dependencies' groups, headed "Deciders": the decision models' servers the picked host knows (a Strands Decider's, or any that answers its System One API), one row each: its name, then, dim and right-aligned, "Running at <its URL>" or why it isn't answering ("Isn't running at http://127.0.0.1:8009"), then Test (a refresh icon: looked at again now) and Remove (a bin). Under them, entry rows Name and URL (http://127.0.0.1:8000 to start with) and a button row "Add Decider", which adds it, looked at at once (a name taken, or a URL that isn't http or https, toasted, the list kept). The host's error, if it can't be asked, in the rows' place. The host's own deciders only: other members' are on their own Settings.

decisions.said: A new part of the SDK that I was unsure of how to incorporate earlier is a decision model SDK… These would be things like strands decider that are picked up on MLX or ollama (wherever you have them hosted). In addition to ask() we would offer decide().
decisions.rule: Every app lets each host's decision-model servers (System One endpoints, such as strands-decider serve) be added, tested and removed in Settings, kept on that host, and a task's script asks one with decide() through its own host and the mesh, never straight to the server's URL; chat models (Ollama's, MLX's) are not deciders

decisions.said: If the model is unavailable, and also bound as a variable, the user gets a warning in advacce. Let the code itself handle the fallback.
decisions.rule: Every host lists each decider with whether it answered when last looked (Decider's reachable, its own and the mesh's), so whatever binds one can warn before a run; decide() raises DecisionUnavailable when its decider can't be asked, and nothing picks another model in its place

decisions.said: Just make the whole thing mate it's not a "step toward decide" I gave you a full proposal and vision and we decided on a plan
decisions.rule: decide() ships whole: the call with typed answers, deciders as hosted models across the mesh, Settings on every app, and availability for typed variables

decisions.said: Think about guidance for installing what Baude depends on (claude, codex, vte3, kubectl, docker) and how Baude behaves when they aren't there (paraphrased)
decisions.rule: Every app lists, per host, what that host's features need and whether it's there, each missing one with the install command for that host's platform, from one table (schema/deps) every app and host reads

decisions.said: Dependencies should say more than installed: whether a kubeconfig is set up and gh is signed in; VTE belongs under Multiplex, Emission needs its own section, Claude Code and Codex go under Providers with MLX's and Ollama's status (paraphrased)
decisions.rule: Every app groups Settings → Dependencies by what needs each dependency (Providers, Git and GitHub, Kubernetes, Databases, Multiplex, Emission, Signal), lists readiness checks beside installs (a kubeconfig with a context, gh signed in, Ollama running with its model count, MLX's model count), each not ready with its fix shown as a missing install's is, and reads all of it from the host

decisions.said: App doesn't detect docker binary on my macOS even though I have Docker installed (paraphrased)
decisions.rule: Every host finds Docker where its installers put it as well as on PATH, since a host started by the OS or an app has a minimal PATH: /usr/local/bin, /opt/homebrew/bin, Docker Desktop's app bundle and ~/.docker/bin, OrbStack's and Rancher Desktop's ~/.orbstack/bin and ~/.rd/bin (Linux: /usr/local/bin, /usr/bin, /snap/bin, ~/.docker/bin, ~/.rd/bin); every run of docker (the Docker view's reads, logs and shells, Databases' containers) uses that found path, and Dependencies says Installed for it

decisions.said: Baude does not find agy in standard locations such as ~/.local/bin (paraphrased)
decisions.rule: Every host finds Antigravity CLI (agy) where its installers put it as well as on PATH, since a host started by the OS or an app has a minimal PATH: ~/.local/bin, ~/.antigravity/antigravity/bin, ~/.antigravity/bin, /opt/homebrew/bin, /usr/local/bin and Antigravity.app on macOS (~/.local/bin, ~/.antigravity/antigravity/bin, ~/.antigravity/bin, /usr/local/bin, /usr/bin and /snap/bin on Linux), with BAUDE_ANTIGRAVITY taking precedence; every check and run of agy (Dependencies, Subscriptions, model discovery, Antigravity chats and sign-in) uses that single lookup

removed.why: Owner: "Drop the kubeconfig setup page nobody is clickigng that shit". A check with no command shows its status only.

removed.name: app's dependencies group
removed.why: The owner asked for the page grouped by what needs each dependency (VTE under Multiplex, an Emission section, Claude Code and Codex under Providers) rather than by host and app; the libraries an app runs itself are listed under those groups, as the viewing app finds them.
